title: improv·artist · naïve (Henri Rousseau)
mutation_directive: improv artist: naïve via Henri Rousseau

improv_extras.practice: untrained jungle paintings; flat foliage, fixed gaze, dreamlike clarity

v1.feedback: The Rousseau concept lands — layered flat foliage with hidden amber eyes is his signature motif, and the deep-canopy greens are perfectly muted. Two refinements: the leaf-shaped point sprites at this density risk reading as a green wash rather than distinct botanical forms; consider using InstancedMesh with flat quad geometry so each leaf has a crisp silhouette with visible midrib, closer to Rousseau's painted-flat style. Second, the eyes could benefit from a very slow pupil dilation cycle (pupR oscillating ±0.02) to heighten the uncanny 'fixed gaze' — right now they pulse brightness but the stare would feel more alive with aperture change.

v2.feedback: Strong Rousseau translation — flat leaf quads with midrib/vein detail and almond-shaped eyes peering through canopy gaps read immediately as the 'fixed gaze through flat foliage' motif. The iris saturation at 0.65 is right at the limit; dropping to 0.45–0.55 with a warmer amber would feel more organic and safer. Consider varying leaf density radially around the eyes more dramatically — right now the peek-holes are subtle at default zoom; a tighter clearing with darker depth-fog behind the eyes would strengthen the 'something watching you' tension. A very slow parallax drift on mouse (not auto-rotate) would add depth to the layered canopy without violating camera rules.
